claims.statement: The active product service runs as decodex serve from the CLI executable, while the macOS bundle contains a decodex helper rather than a separate decodexd executable.
GPUI supervises its bundled service through a parent-lifetime channel, while typed clients reject incompatible protocol versions instead of opening product storage directly.
The macOS stage test verifies bundle payloads, signing, metadata and native ABI compatibility, including rejection of an incompatible fixture.

The attested native launch requests subagent context defaults, Agent message wakeups and full-fork prefix preservation without enabling multi_agent_v2 itself or forcing gRPC hosting; code_mode_tool_description_first is accepted as a removed native feature.
Native shutdown refusal classification uses code -32600 and serverShuttingDown data, permits the exact older message only when data is absent, and does not itself authorize replay.

The source-runtime builder verifies an exact official upstream archive URL and digest, recreates its extracted source cache, builds with stable Rust and the locked upstream Cargo graph, stamps the selected commit, and rejects Cargo-lock or package-identity changes.
The source-runtime builder signs CodexCLI.app, the Code Mode helper, rg and any advertised standalone executor, then verifies their strict signatures.

The component store verifies package signatures and the reported CLI version, generates schemas from the actual executable, checks its executable and schema hashes, and records the requirement in the installed component directory.
The source extractor replaces the owned source cache and refreshes file modification times instead of restoring archived timestamps, while preserving the Cargo build directory for dependency reuse.

Development artifact preparation is explicit and retains the reviewed source commit and schema, while production staging selects an official release whose qualification covers the development baseline; neither app startup nor staging compiles Codex.
The shared component store retries failed downloads three times and atomically publishes verified replacements, retaining older versions and the previous directory when repair fails.

The app lifecycle prepares its pinned component before the owned local service connects without consuming connection retry attempts. Settings > Components exposes runtime preparation and native optional EGM lifecycle; Settings > Updates retains Sparkle application updates.
Decodex resolves native child requests through a verified native parent chain and does not own a second local child-admission lifecycle.

Context defaults keeps saved user values separate from effective project configuration. An omitted context feature uses defaultEnabled from the native feature catalog, while explicit effective configuration takes priority. Writes use native file-version compare-and-swap and readback without a startup force-enable argument or duplicate SQLite preference.

The context settings UI shows effective project and explicit user defaults separately, applies preferences to new conversations without restarting loaded ones, preserves the existing async threshold table by editing its enabled leaf, and does not automatically resend an unconfirmed write.
Compatibility delegation instructions can request native tool-output retention, while wakes, capacity retries and external evidence remain unselected; retention does not replace durable Work records.

Startup version and schema preflights reserve one bounded cleanup slot before spawning and retain the daemon capacity owner through both preflights; this unbound ProcessGuard does not create an account RunnerPermit.

When immediate child cleanup cannot finish, ProcessGroupOwner transfers the child, output pump and cleanup guard to the reaper, and the profile regression covers this handoff during either preflight phase.

The portable qualification record binds native artifact and helper identities to explicit limits; the stable retained contract catalog stores separate installed development acceptance with its own application identity and scope.

Repository-owned model-error and large-catalog fixtures check terminal modelNotFound classification and explicit catalogs larger than 1 MiB with an exact CLI. Current qualification identifies the executed fixtures; historical executions keep their original artifact limits.

Project, Agent and Work remain separate durable business objects; native Codex owns execution, while scoped commands, Collaboration and optional native Guardian review records remain in Decodex without a global permission override.
Protocol 4.7 accepts one exact major and minor revision and retains publication-instance receipts for reconnect and idempotent recovery.
Selected Work evidence uses digest-checked bounded pages and applies Agent and granted Material scope before database record limits.

The current schema retains exact native child-input identity independently of parent activity, allowing permitted nested V2 Work attribution and recovery without replay while preserving direct and V1 paths and explicit Unknown states.

The runtime reconciles retained native Project membership after exact hydration and before input, assigns only unassigned threads, and parks conflicts without switching execution directory or permissions or blocking independent Agents.
An independent Agent can bootstrap from a real pending first user input without an Assistant, and each native conversation attaches only to the admitted process that created or resumed it.

The current schema preserves process ownership and distinguishes plaintext assignment proof from native task-name proof; exact native metadata and activity can recover named encrypted assignments without replay or a claim that the prompt was decrypted.
Completed Guardian reviews can trigger bounded read-only history recovery after cold resume, preserving verified parent identity and explicit gaps without deciding or replaying an action.
The selected memory, collaboration history and actual usage views use read-only projections of native memory and retained source records, without adding an executor or automatically accepting Work.

Side chats reuse the prompt-fork journal, exact source Agent parent and retained Project, role and provider identity; creation copies no native Goal and sends no input. Unknown outcomes require recovery of the retained receipt without replay.

The attached-branch query bounds retained Decodex receipts to the newest 100 for an exact source. Native archive observation uses exact attachment filters and source binding; incomplete discovery remains unknown.
Permission, dotenv startup and policyCapacityUnavailable requirements retain their historical fixture and source-inclusion evidence; current affected checks and historical executions remain separate.

Settings > Agents and Agent preferences share the native defaults controls. The MCP switch edits only startup_readiness for an existing writable user server, using catalog or connection and the same source/version-bound write/readback. It exposes names and readiness without credentials and does not implement cache or connection policy.

The standalone Codex startup-configuration diagnostic UI, local query and dedicated qualification helper are retired. Decodex retains product/integration diagnostics, ordinary warnings and conversation Markdown export; this does not qualify an installed protocol 4.0 application against the current service.

Read-only nearby-history and registered-resource-owner queries reuse native source ownership, exact identities and native cursors, discard changed sources, and add no local history or file-association store.

The desktop reuses an already loaded exact native item without GetItemContext; an unloaded item uses the existing query and message/tool renderers in the main transcript. The bounded item window has identity-based presentation anchors rather than fabricated canonical timeline ordinals, remains separate from the cached ordinary page, and offers a fixed return to the prior reading position.
Shared component verification requires the exact advertised executor path, verifies its signature and fixed development commit, and preserves legacy packages without execServer metadata.

The development lock and current qualification identify the qualified fixed source and signed artifact. Historical probes retain their original limits. HumanCommand remains deferred and unadvertised; runtime selection does not install the app or resume the automation.
Provider recovery requires a live native mismatch and a matching current configuration, then reuses the durable explicit fork without sending input or mutating the source.
The selected native runtime includes retained reasoning after incomplete or usage-less responses in context accounting before automatic compaction; Decodex uses the native result.

The Agent host runs title inference after eligible completed user exchanges through isolated ephemeral structured requests. Native connection-owned private routing is shared with recaps; source conversations receive no title-generation turn.

Resolved conversation_title observations retain native-name provenance and successful review checkpoints in the existing indexed journal without wakes or transcript rows. Work snapshots read the current binding and topic map in one SQLite transaction, separately from Agent identity and Work titles.
Native connection-owned private routes retain temporary thread state and cleanup observations while excluding those events from foreground question, review and timing observations.
Native name revisions use a separate guard: manual renames invalidate outstanding title writes without invalidating task permission or model observations or an existing Recap.

Assistant settings, teams, independent wakes and exact native context/import receipts reuse the existing Inbox journal without a schema change or a second executor. Context renewal preserves the stable Agent and Work, and RAGFlow imports run as one bounded background job on the existing host tick.

RAGFlow Install prepares the managed nightly service and private account. User model configuration accepts an OpenAI-compatible Base URL, optional API key and custom extraction and embedding names; native verification precedes saving, then dedicated Memory is created or recovered. No model runtime, download or data volume is installed. The origin-bound RAGFlow credential stays private; Assistant settings contain only its reference and chat import starts disabled.

RAGFlow lifecycle operations address one per-user Docker Compose project with a loopback-only API. Update records actual installed version and image readback while retaining models, credentials, import choice and data. Uninstall stops only that project, clears the Assistant connection and retains data volumes for reinstall.

The ARM64 Infinity runtime uses the official compatible 0.7.4 binary and analyzer resources on Ubuntu 24.04, built from a context that contains only its Dockerfile and excludes the component account and Compose credentials.

The model endpoint path is preserved and loopback host names are translated to host.docker.internal for the owned container while the displayed URL stays unchanged. A Memory with messages cannot silently change its embedding model or endpoint; model verification failures preserve the saved component configuration.
